marta: Quick follow-up on the incremental admit adapter RFC — want to nail the tradeoffs for eager vs lazy compatibility checks before we land the refactor. TL;DR: propose a lightweight inline smoke + async deep bench flow. feedback pls by EOD :hourglass: 

jia: Agree on hybrid. Eager/full checks catch regressions early but slow down intake. Lazy async checks reduce onboarding latency but leave a window where a bad model can be served. Hybrid looks like best balance.

ryan: From runtime benching: full bench (1000 samples + kv cache sim) on a single node adds ~40–60s to ingest if done serially. If we parallelize across 8 runners that drops to ~8s per model but uses more infra. Example command we use for local sims:

```
run_bench --model-path s3://models/x --samples 1000 --kv-sim --parallel 8
```

samir: Cost/ops perspective: parallel heavy benches are fine but we should avoid them by default for every PR. Proposed policy: 
- Inline smoke (<= 2m): latency, basic top-1 correctness, kv-cache basic ops. block on this.
- Async deep bench (scheduled on cluster): full perplexity + latency tail + quant/ops compatibility. report-only by default; can be blocking for "critical" models/tags.

jia: Small API suggestion for the admit adapter return so tools can make deterministic decisions: 
```
AdmitResponse = {
  status: "accepted" | "deferred" | "rejected",
  fingerprints: ["kv-hash", "model-bin-hash"],
  warnings: ["quantization-diff:0.12", "kv-warmup-variance"],
  bench_report_url: "s3://..."
}
```
We need to persist `fingerprints` and `bench_report_url` to the model registry so downstream routing can fallback to compatible variants.

marta: Prefer keeping the inline contract minimal. Maybe `status`, `fingerprints`, and `report` link only. Warnings should be surfaced to UI but not part of blocking contract. Operationally:
- Block if inline smoke => `status: rejected`
- Otherwise `status: deferred` and async job runs.
- For `critical` tag, mark an admission flag that prevents serving until async job transitions to `accepted` (this is the canary mode).

samir: One more infra note — we should tag async jobs with the originating commit/model-id and ensure retries are idempotent. Also plumb cost center metadata so billing for heavy benches is visible.

jia: On KV compatibility tests: we should include deterministic warmup sequence + short TTL churn test. Catch regressions in cache evictions. small snippet:
```
# pseudo
for seq in golden_seq:
  send(seq)
assert hit_rate > 0.85
```

ryan: Will prototype a parallel runner that can run the deep bench in a k8s job with configurable concurrency. If we go this route, we can afford heavier async benches and keep inline checks cheap.

oncall-bot: Note: scheduled deep-bench capacity is limited tonight 02:00-06:00 UTC for maintenance window. Jobs queued may start after window ends.

marta: Decision outline for RFC follow-up (I will update the RFC w/ this):
1) Inline smoke (<=2m) — blocking on intake.
2) Async deep bench — non-blocking by default, blocking if `critical` flag set.
3) AdmitResponse contract minimal (status, fingerprints, report_url). Warnings surfaced to UI and notes.
4) Persist fingerprints + report link to registry.
5) Parallel deep-bench runner prototype tracked as separate deliverable.

Can folks react with :+1: if this matches your understanding, or drop a short objection. I want to finalize before EOD.

jia: :+1:

ryan: +1, will start prototyping the k8s runner tomorrow.

samir: +1 — will add cost tagging and idempotency hooks.

marta: Thanks everyone :rocket:
